Question Choices: Select. A crayon is 4 inches long. A pencil is about twice as long as the crayon. About how long is the pencil?: ~~8-inches | 2-inches | 20-inches | 4-inches~~
Hints: Twice as long means 2 times the length.
Solution: Twice as long means two equal lengths. Add 4+4 = 8 inches. Select 8-inches.

Question Choices: Select. Two identical books each measure about 8 inches from top to bottom. Lay them flat and end to end so these lengths touch without overlapping. About how many inches long is the combined length? ~~16-inches | 8-inches | 4-inches | 10-inches~~
Hints: Add the two equal top-to-bottom lengths.
Solution: Each book contributes 8 inches along the same line. Add the two lengths: 8 + 8 = 16 inches. The books touch end to end, so there is no gap or overlap.

Question Choices: Select. A door is 3 feet wide. A window is half as wide as the door. How wide is the window? ~~1-foot | 1.5-feet | 6-feet | 5-feet~~
Hints: Split 3 feet into two equal lengths. Each is one and a half feet.
Solution: Half of 3 feet is 1.5 feet, or one and a half feet. Check: 1.5 + 1.5 = 3. The old choices of 1 foot and 2 feet were equally far from the exact value, so neither was uniquely closest.

Question Choices: Select. A tree is 10 meters tall. A bush next to it looks about half as tall. About how tall is the bush?: ~~5m | 10m | 20m | 1m~~
Solution: The bush is about half the 10-meter tree height. Two groups of 5 make 10, so select 5m.

Question Choices: Select. A table is about 40 inches long. A chair next to it looks much shorter. About how long is the chair?: ~~20-inches | 40-inches | 60-inches~~
Hints: The chair must be a smaller number than the table.
Solution: The chair is much shorter than 40 inches. Of the choices, only 20 inches is shorter; 40 is equal and 60 is longer. Select 20-inches.
